readings.title: The Priestly Ministry Begins
readings.subtitle: Aaron's Offerings for Himself and the People
readings.text: [Leviticus 9:1] And it came to be on the eighth day that Mosheh called Aharon and his sons and the elders of Yisra’ĕl. [2] And he said to Aharon, “Take for yourself a young bull as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering, perfect ones, and bring them before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [3] “And speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Take a kid of the goats as a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, both a year old, perfect ones, as a burnt offering, [4] and a bull and a ram as peace offerings to slaughter before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and a grain offering mixed with oil. For today <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall appear to you.’ ” [5] And they brought what Mosheh commanded before the Tent of Meeting. And all the congregation drew near and stood before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [6] And Mosheh said, “This is the word which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded you to do, so that the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appears to you.” [7] And Mosheh said to Aharon, “Draw near to the altar, and prepare your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people. And prepare the offering of the people, and make atonement for them, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded.” [8] And Aharon drew near to the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering, which was for himself. [9] And the sons of Aharon brought the blood to him. And he dipped his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar, and poured the blood at the base of the altar. [10] And the fat and the kidneys and the appendage on the liver of the sin offering he burned on the altar, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had commanded Mosheh. [11] And the flesh and the skin he burned with fire outside the camp. [12] And he slaughtered the burnt offering. And the sons of Aharon presented the blood to him, which he sprinkled on the altar all around. [13] And they presented the burnt offering to him, with its pieces and the head, and he burned them on the altar. [14] And he washed the entrails and the legs, and burned them on the burnt offering on the altar. [15] And he brought the people’s offering, and took the goat, which was the sin offering for the people, and slaughtered it and offered it for sin, like the first one. [16] And he brought the burnt offering and prepared it according to the right ruling. [17] And he brought the grain offering, and filled his hand with it, and burned it on the altar, besides the burnt offering of the morning. [18] And he slaughtered the bull and the ram as a slaughtering of peace offerings, which was for the people. And the sons of Aharon presented the blood to him, which he sprinkled on the altar all around, [19] and the fat from the bull and the ram, the fat tail, and what covers the entrails, and the kidneys, and the appendage on the liver. [20] And they put the fat on the breasts, and he burned the fat on the altar, [21] but the breasts and the right thigh Aharon waved as a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, as Mosheh had commanded. [22] And Aharon lifted up his hand toward the people and blessed them, and came down from preparing the sin offering, and the burnt offering, and the peace offerings. [23] And Mosheh and Aharon went into the Tent of Meeting, and came out and blessed the people. And the esteem of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to all the people, [24] and fire came out from before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and consumed the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. And when all the people saw it, they shouted and fell on their faces.

readings.title: Strange Fire
readings.subtitle: The Death of Nadab and Abihu
readings.text: [Leviticus 10:1] And Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aharon, each took his fire holder and put fire in it, and put incense on it, and brought strange fire before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which <dn>He</dn> had not commanded them. [2] And fire came out from <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and consumed them, and they died before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [3] And Mosheh said to Aharon, “This is what <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke, saying, <dq>‘By those who come near <dn>Me</dn> let <dn>Me</dn> be set apart! And before all the people let <dn>Me</dn> be esteemed!’</dq> ” And Aharon was silent. [4] And Mosheh called Misha’ĕl and Eltsaphan, the sons of Uzzi’ĕl the uncle of Aharon, and said to them, “Come near, take your brothers from before the Set-apart Place out of the camp.” [5] So they came near and took them by their long shirts out of the camp, as Mosheh had said. [6] And Mosheh said to Aharon, and to El‘azar and Ithamar, his sons, “Do not unbind your heads nor tear your garments, lest you die, and wrath come upon all the congregation. But let your brothers, the entire house of Yisra’ĕl, bewail the burning which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has kindled. [7] “And do not go out from the door of the Tent of Meeting, lest you die, for the anointing oil of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is upon you.” And they did according to the word of Mosheh.

readings.title: Laws for the Priests
readings.subtitle: Holiness and Consumption of Offerings
readings.text: [Leviticus 10:8] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Aharon, saying, [9] <dq>“Do not drink wine or strong drink, you, nor your sons with you, when you go into the Tent of Meeting, lest you die. It is a law forever throughout your generations,</dq> [10] <dq>so as to distinguish between the set-apart and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean,</dq> [11] <dq>and to teach the children of Yisra’ĕl all the laws which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken to them by the hand of Mosheh.”</dq> [12] And Mosheh spoke to Aharon, and to El‘azar and Ithamar, his sons who were left, “Take the grain offering that remains of the offerings made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for it is most set-apart. [13] “And you shall eat it in a set-apart place, because it is your portion and your sons’ portion, of the offerings made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. For so I have been commanded. [14] “And the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution you eat in a clean place, you, and your sons, and your daughters with you. For they are your portion and your sons’ portion, which are given from the slaughterings of peace offerings of the children of Yisra’ĕl. [15] “The thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering they bring with the offerings of fat made by fire, to bring as a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And it shall be yours and your sons’ with you, by a law forever, as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has commanded.” [16] And Mosheh diligently sought the goat of the sin offering, and see, it was burned up! And he was angry with El‘azar and Ithamar, the sons of Aharon who were left, saying, [17] “Why have you not eaten the sin offering in a set-apart place, since it is most set-apart, and <dn>He</dn> has given it to you to bear the crookedness of the congregation, to make atonement for them before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>? [18] “See, its blood was not brought inside the Set-apart Place. You should have eaten it in a set-apart place, as I commanded.” [19] And Aharon said to Mosheh, “See, today they have brought their sin offering and their burnt offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and matters like these have befallen me! If I had eaten the sin offering today, would it have been good in the eyes of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>?” [20] And when Mosheh heard that, it was good in his eyes.

readings.title: Clean and Unclean Creatures
readings.subtitle: Dietary Laws for Holiness
readings.text: [Leviticus 11:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh and to Aharon, saying to them, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘These are the living creatures which you do eat among all the beasts that are on the earth:</dq> [3] <dq>‘Whatever has a split hoof completely divided, chewing the cud, among the beasts, that you do eat.</dq> [4] <dq>‘Only, these you do not eat among those that chew the cud or those that have a split hoof: the camel, because it chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, it is unclean to you;</dq> [5] <dq>and the rabbit, because it chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, it is unclean to you;</dq> [6] <dq>and the hare, because it chews the cud but does not have a split hoof, it is unclean to you;</dq> [7] <dq>and the pig, though it has a split hoof, completely divided, yet does not chew the cud, it is unclean to you.</dq> [8] <dq>‘Their flesh you do not eat, and their carcasses you do not touch. They are unclean to you.</dq> [9] <dq>‘These you do eat of all that are in the waters: any one that has fins and scales in the waters, in the seas or in the rivers, that you do eat.</dq> [10] <dq>‘But all that have not fins and scales in the seas and in the rivers, all that move in the waters or any living creature which is in the waters, they are an abomination to you.</dq> [11] <dq>‘They are an abomination to you – of their flesh you do not eat, and their carcasses you abominate.</dq> [12] <dq>‘All that have not fins and scales in the waters is an abomination to you.</dq> [13] <dq>‘And these you abominate among the birds, they are not eaten, they are an abomination: the eagle, and the vulture, and the black vulture,</dq> [14] <dq>and the hawk, and the falcon after its kind,</dq> [15] <dq>every raven after its kind,</dq> [16] <dq>and the ostrich, and the nighthawk, and the seagull, and the hawk after its kind,</dq> [17] <dq>and the little owl, and the fisher owl, and the great owl,</dq> [18] <dq>and the white owl, and the pelican, and the carrion vulture,</dq> [19] <dq>and the stork, the heron after its kind, and the hoopoe, and the bat.</dq> [20] <dq>‘All flying insects that creep on all fours is an abomination to you.</dq> [21] <dq>‘Only, these you do eat of every flying insect that creeps on all fours: those which have jointed legs above their feet with which to leap on the earth.</dq> [22] <dq>‘These of them you do eat: the locust after its kind, and the destroying locust after its kind, and the cricket after its kind, and the grasshopper after its kind.</dq> [23] <dq>‘But all other flying insects which have four feet is an abomination to you.</dq> [24] <dq>‘And by these you are made unclean, anyone touching their carcass is unclean until evening;</dq> [25] <dq>and anyone picking up part of their carcass washes his garments, and shall be unclean until evening.</dq> [26] <dq>‘Every beast which has a split hoof not completely divided, or does not chew the cud, is unclean to you. Anyone who touches them is unclean.</dq> [27] <dq>‘And whatever goes on its paws, among all the kinds of living creatures that go on all fours, those are unclean to you. Anyone who touches their carcass is unclean until evening.</dq> [28] <dq>‘And he who picks up their carcass washes his garments, and shall be unclean until evening. They are unclean to you.</dq> [29] <dq>‘And these are unclean to you among the creeping creatures that creep on the earth: the mole, and the mouse, and the tortoise after its kind,</dq> [30] <dq>and the gecko, and the land crocodile, and the sand reptile, and the sand lizard, and the chameleon.</dq> [31] <dq>‘These are unclean to you among all that creep. Anyone who touches them when they are dead is unclean until evening.</dq> [32] <dq>‘And whatever any of them falls on when they are dead, it is unclean, whether it is any vessel of wood, or garment, or skin, or sack, any vessel used for work, it is put in water. And it shall be unclean until evening, then it is clean.</dq> [33] <dq>‘And any earthen vessel into which any of them falls, whatever is in it is unclean, and you break it.</dq> [34] <dq>‘Any food that is eaten, on which water comes, is unclean. And any drink that is drunk, in any such vessel, is unclean.</dq> [35] <dq>‘And on whatever any part of their carcass falls it is unclean. An oven or cooking range is broken down, they are unclean, and are unclean to you.</dq> [36] <dq>‘But a fountain or a well, a collection of water, is clean. But he who touches their carcass is unclean.</dq> [37] <dq>‘And if any part of their carcass falls on any planting seed which is to be sown, it is clean.</dq> [38] <dq>‘But if water is put on the seed, and any part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean to you.</dq> [39] <dq>‘And when any beast which is for food for you dies, he who touches its carcass is unclean until evening.</dq> [40] <dq>‘And he who eats of its carcass washes his garments, and shall be unclean until evening. And he who picks up its carcass washes his garments, and shall be unclean until evening.</dq> [41] <dq>‘And every creeping creature that creeps on the earth is an abomination, it is not eaten.</dq> [42] <dq>‘Whatever crawls on its belly, and whatever goes on all fours, or whatever has many feet among all creeping creatures that creep on the earth, these you do not eat, for they are an abomination.</dq> [43] <dq>‘Do not make yourselves abominable with any creeping creature that creeps, and do not make yourselves unclean with them, lest you be defiled by them.</dq> [44] <dq>‘For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and you shall set yourselves apart. And you shall be set-apart, for <dn>I</dn> am set-apart. And do not defile your beings with any creeping creature that creeps on the earth.</dq> [45] <dq>‘For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who is bringing you up out of the land of Mitsrayim, to be your <dn>Elohim</dn>. And you shall be set-apart, for <dn>I</dn> am set-apart.</dq> [46] <dq>‘This is the Torah of the beasts and the birds and every living creature that moves in the waters, and of every creature that creeps on the earth,</dq> [47] <dq>to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creature that is to be eaten and the living creature that is not to be eaten.’ ”</dq>
